claims.text: Adding 1–3 at.% Y2O3 nanoparticles to MoNbTaW will improve high-temperature mechanical strength relative to undoped MoNbTaW.
Adding 1–3 at.% Y2O3 nanoparticles to MoNbTaW will improve irradiation resistance relative to undoped MoNbTaW.
The oxide addition will not compromise the thermal stability of MoNbTaW.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering will produce a uniform nanoscale dispersion of Y2O3 particles in MoNbTaW.
Nanoscale Y2O3 particles will obstruct dislocation motion in MoNbTaW.
Nanoscale Y2O3 particles will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects in MoNbTaW.
The oxide particles will strengthen the alloy by impeding dislocation glide through Orowan strengthening.
Y2O3 particles will absorb or interact with irradiation-induced point defects and small defect clusters.
Interactions between Y2O3 particles and irradiation defects will reduce defect accumulation and coarsening.
At 1200°C, yield strength and hardness will be at least 20% higher than in identically processed undoped MoNbTaW.
After irradiation, swelling will be reduced by at least 15% relative to undoped MoNbTaW.
After irradiation, hardening will be reduced by at least 15% relative to undoped MoNbTaW.
No significant grain growth will occur at 1000–1400°C and under heavy-ion irradiation up to 10 dpa.
No significant Y2O3 nanoparticle coarsening will occur at 1000–1400°C and under heavy-ion irradiation up to 10 dpa.
Oxide contents above 5 at.% may cause embrittlement and diminish effectiveness.
Nanoparticle sizes above 50 nm may diminish the beneficial effect.
The benefits may not persist above 1500°C because of particle coarsening.
The magnitude of improvement depends on nanoparticle dispersion quality and oxide–matrix interface stability.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least 20% strength/hardness improvement and 15% reductions in swelling and hardening, whereas the falsification rule uses only 10% thresholds and an ambiguous 'or' condition. Results between these thresholds could fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
